properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 15 at 2:58AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves of 22 to 25 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte and Northern Coastal Humboldt
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST early this morning. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement early this
morning, another large swell is forecast to arrive to the
shoreline late Sunday through Monday.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 15 at 1:38AM PST until November 15 at 4:45AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Del Norte County in northwestern California...

* WHEN...Until 445 AM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 137 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Crescent City, Jedediah Smith State Park, Bertsch-Oceanview,
Crescent City North, Smith River and Fort Dick.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding. Drive slow in flood-prone areas.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 15 at 12:55AM PST until November 15 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...Most of the Shasta Valley in central Siskiyou County. This
includes portions of Interstate 5 as well as the communities of
Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and driving may become difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways running west to east will be exposed
to tough driving conditions given the strong southerly wind speeds.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects, including large or
inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or damaged
by the wind.

properties.description:

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion.

dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 15 at 12:29AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at
favored breakpoints. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking
waves of 20 to 25 ft, with occasional sets of 25 to 35 ft at
favored breakpoints.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST today. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM today through 4 AM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.
Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, breaking waves of 5 to 8
feet. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. Minor tidal overflows
are possible during high tides.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, from 4 AM PST Sunday through
Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.Surf will we highest for west- northwest facing
beaches.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce elevated surf
into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking today and potentially again Monday. Minor tidal
overflows are possible in areas with largest surf, especially
during high tide.
properties.instruction:

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 8:26PM PST until November 17 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For
the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an
exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal
structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 8:26PM PST until November 17 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
12 feet, lowering to 7 to 10 feet on Sunday. Occasional larger
sets may occur near Ventura Harbor. Dangerous rip currents
expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible.
There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to
moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially
when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these
impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
